name: 1729 Prairie Avenue — the Pullman estate's stable and one-storey ranges (the district draft's massing, kept by T-1880; refined by T-1934)

grade.why: Pictured: a picture on the Images tab shows it.

documented_range.note: The draft claims the 1904 target and no more: the 1911 sheet draws the building and the T-1840 census rules it present in 1904 (present_as_mapped). Its building and loss dates are the per-building ticket's to read.

placement.position_note: The rear corner of the main body's rectangle (lot frame u 43.750, v -3.500 m from the middle of the rear lot line), through the T-1250 fit of the sheet: the sheet's georeference carries no independent check, so its own fit residual, 3.08 m RMS on its control crossings, is all that is claimed. Rotation 179.611 degrees turns the plan's u axis onto the lot's own rear-to-street line.
placement.symbolic_location: 1729 S. Prairie Avenue, parcel prairie_1729 (data/street_grid/1904.json), east side of Prairie Avenue, Prairie Avenue, 16th to 18th Street (Sanborn 1911 vol. 3 sheet 20).

footprint.note: The stable block: the draft's rectangle 2 of the traced main part (s20fp-1729-b1 p3), in the Pullman house draft's frame (u toward Prairie Avenue, v south), which this record keeps; the other two parts are in draft_plan.

stories.note: '2' printed on the 1911 sheet over the east building (GARAGE); the ranges are one storey ('1B', '1').

construction.note: The register reads the map's colours as 'stone'.

parts.from: s20fp-1729-b1 p3 (main, stone), the draft's rectangle 2 (the east building, lettered GARAGE)
s20fp-1729-b1 p3 (main, stone), the draft's rectangle 3 (the 1B range north of the house's rear), stopped at the K01 house's north wall
s20fp-1729-b1 p4 (range, stone), the porte-cochere marked '1', stopped at the K01 house's 18th Street pavilion

draft_plan.note: The draft's rectangles (cell 0.25 m, at most 3 a part) that the K01 house does not carry, in the Pullman house draft's frame: the east building at two storeys as the draft stood it (wing_storeys), the 1B range and the porte-cochere at one storey under flat roofs, as the sheet letters them. Roofs per piece are the draft rules' (reconstructed).

draft_elevation.note: RECONSTRUCTED: the draft rules' service elevation (as the district's coach houses take it), written by T-1880 for the stable and ranges the Pullman house's draft carried; heights are the rules' starting values inside RECONSTRUCTION-RULES.md's ranges. Liberty L-draft-prairie-16-18-east-2335.

function.note: The 1911 sheet's two-storey building at the lot's east end, lettered GARAGE (a 1911 use), with the one-and-a-half-storey part beside it, where the estate's stable stood (the Inland Architect's 1894 plate of the palm house and stable); the one-storey ranges are the sheet's 1B range north of the house's rear and the one-storey porte-cochere on 18th Street.

built.note: The marker: 'George M. Pullman Residence. Built 1870-1876'.

citations.citation: 'Lost Houses of Prairie Avenue: 1600-1700 Blocks', Prairie Avenue Historic District interpretive marker, Chicago; transcription on the Historical Marker Database (HMdb), marker 308722.
what_it_supplies: each house's builder, year built and architect as the district's marker gives them
Pullman's theatre, organ and bowling alley and Beman's conservatory additions, in paraphrase

citations.citation: Sanborn Map Company. Insurance Maps of Chicago, Illinois, Volume 3. New York: Sanborn Map Company, 1911. Sheet 20.
what_it_supplies: The Illinois Central / Michigan Central right-of-way and, from the 16th Street row south about 60 m, the water's edge beside it, as of 1911
Footprints, lot lines, street widths (66 ft; 16th Street 50 ft), addresses, material by colour and story counts for Indiana Av. to the tracks, 16th to 18th Street, as of 1911
Its own printed Scale of Feet, which the georeference uses as its scale
what_it_does_not_supply: Anything as of 1904 on its own authority. It is a 1911 survey; Glessner House's reading that everything on sheets 20, 28 and 35 but 1609-1611 and 1620 Prairie stood in 1904 is attributed guidance, recorded in that README, and not checked by this record
A construction date for any building it draws
Elevations, grades, curb heights or fill depths -- no Sanborn sheet carries a level
Architecture above the footprint beyond its story count, material colour and roof symbol
The lake edge beyond the stretch the sheet actually inks: the pen line stops while the tracks run on

research_note: The parts of the 1911 sheet's trace s20fp-1729-b1 that the Pullman house's K01 record (pullman_house_1729_prairie, T-1880) does not carry, kept where and as the district draft (T-2335) stood them so that nothing the sheet draws goes missing while the house moves onto K01: the stable and garage block at the lot's east end at two storeys, the 1B range north of the house's rear at one storey, and the porte-cochere on 18th Street at one storey. K01's wings stand on the main block's rear wall, and these do not (the conservatory, its own K13 record, stands between). Written by T-1880 on the draft builder from the draft's own rectangles, not by the draft rules (the rules' skip names it); every height, roof and opening is the draft rules' reconstruction (liberty L-draft-prairie-16-18-east-2335). T-1934 refines it.
